messages:
acme-admin: Hey team — after installing Redwood Private agent in our `redwood` namespace we see the agent stuck in CrashLoopBackOff and can't register. Getting API timeouts from our app. Can someone help?

lina (support): Sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste `kubectl -n redwood get pods` and the agent pod logs?

acme-admin: Here: `kubectl -n redwood get pods`
```
redwood-agent-0   0/1   CrashLoopBackOff   5   3m
```
Logs from `kubectl -n redwood logs redwood-agent-0`:
```
2026-03-17T10:12:05Z agent INFO starting
2026-03-17T10:12:08Z agent WARN dns lookup failed: lookup control-plane.prod.redwood.cloud: no such host
2026-03-17T10:12:08Z agent ERROR dial tcp: lookup control-plane.prod.redwood.cloud: no such host
```

lina (support): Looks like DNS resolution to our control-plane host is failing. Are you using a default-deny NetworkPolicy or an egress firewall?

acme-admin: We do have a CiliumNetworkPolicy default deny for the namespace (security requirement). But we allowed egress to our internal APIs only.

sam (eng-infra): Two quick checks: 1) can the agent pod reach your cluster DNS? `kubectl -n redwood exec -it redwood-agent-0 -- nslookup control-plane.prod.redwood.cloud` and 2) can it reach 8.8.8.8:53/udp or your on-cluster kube-dns IP?

acme-admin: Ran them, output:
```
$ kubectl -n redwood exec -it redwood-agent-0 -- nslookup control-plane.prod.redwood.cloud
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached

$ kubectl -n redwood exec -it redwood-agent-0 -- cat /etc/resolv.conf
nameserver 10.96.0.10
search redwood.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local
options ndots:5
```

lina (support): Ok DNS isn't answering from the pod. That explains the `no such host`. Because you have a default-deny CNP, you need an explicit egress allow to the cluster DNS (UDP/TCP 53 to 10.96.0.10) and to the Redwood control-plane endpoints (TCP 443) or to the egress proxy if you use one.

jules (eng-runtime): Also confirm if your cluster egress is constrained at the node or CNI level (Cilium EgressFirewall / CiliumNetworkPolicy). If there's an egress allowlist, the agent won't be able to fetch CRL/OCSP or TLS SNI endpoints and will fail later even if DNS works.

acme-admin: We use Cilium CNP. Our security team only wanted to allow egress to internal subnets. How do we write the rule to allow DNS + Redwood without opening everything?

sam (eng-infra): Example minimal CiliumNetworkPolicy allow egress (adjust target IPs/FQDNs as needed):
```
apiVersion: cilium.io/v2
kind: CiliumNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-redwood-agent-egress
  namespace: redwood
spec:
  endpointSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redwood-agent
  egress:
  - toEndpoints:
    - matchLabels:
        k8s-app: kube-dns
    toPorts:
    - ports:
      - port: "53"
        protocol: UDP
  - toFQDNs:
    - matchName: "control-plane.prod.redwood.cloud"
    toPorts:
    - ports:
      - port: "443"
        protocol: TCP
```

lina (support): If your Cilium version doesn't support `toFQDNs`, you can add IP ranges for our control-plane region. We can provide the IP block — pinging eng-runtime.

jules (eng-runtime): We publish public control-plane IP ranges for customers on private deployments. For this customer's region the control-plane uses: `34.82.10.0/24` and `34.82.11.0/24`. Also the agent needs egress to your DNS (10.96.0.10) and to CRL/OCSP hosts (we'll list if you get TLS errors).

acme-admin: Applied the CNP allowing kube-dns and the two IP ranges. After restart agent logs now show TLS handshake but then timeouts:
```
2026-03-17T10:19:02Z agent INFO connecting to https://control-plane.prod.redwood.cloud:443
2026-03-17T10:19:05Z agent ERROR tls handshake timeout
```

lina (support): TLS handshake timeout often means there's an egress HTTP proxy or firewall doing TLS interception, or the node/nat gateway blocks 443. Could you try `kubectl -n redwood exec -it redwood-agent-0 -- curl -v --resolve control-plane.prod.redwood.cloud:443:34.82.10.12 https://control-plane.prod.redwood.cloud/health` and paste output?

acme-admin: Output:
```
* Rebuilt URL to: https://control-plane.prod.redwood.cloud/health
*   Trying 34.82.10.12...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* connect to 34.82.10.12 port 443 failed: Operation timed out
* Failed to connect to control-plane.prod.redwood.cloud port 443: Operation timed out
```

sam (eng-infra): That indicates packets to the control-plane IPs are being dropped or blocked by a firewall/NAT gateway on your side. Since DNS is now working, this is not a DNS issue. Check cloud provider security groups, node egress rules, and any VPC egress ACLs. Also ensure iptables on nodes don't DROP outbound 443.

acme-admin: We're on-prem with a perimeter firewall that does allow 443 out but only to a proxy IP. Is there a way to configure the agent to use an outbound HTTP proxy?

jules (eng-runtime): Agent supports HTTPS proxy via env vars `HTTPS_PROXY` / `https_proxy` in the DaemonSet. If you must go through an outbound proxy, set those envs and allowlist the proxy IP to reach our control-plane IPs. Example snippet for the agent DaemonSet env: `- name: HTTPS_PROXY value: "https://10.1.2.3:3128"`

acme-admin: We'll try that and open firewall to the proxy IP. One more thing — our security team asks for a minimal list of destinations to allow (DNS, control-plane IPs). Can you confirm a short list?

lina (support): Minimum allowlist: - Cluster DNS IP (UDP/TCP 53) - Our control-plane IP ranges for your region (we listed two above: `34.82.10.0/24`, `34.82.11.0/24`) - If you use a proxy, allow the proxy to connect to those ranges - If you see TLS cert validation errors later, also allow CRL/OCSP hosts (we'll provide specific hostnames on request).

acme-admin: Thanks — applying proxy env and firewall rule now. Will report back. :pray:

deploy-bot: redwood-agent-0 restarted (image: redwood/agent:v1.8.2)

acme-admin: After adding HTTPS_PROXY and allowing proxy → control-plane ranges, agent connected successfully and registration completed. App errors cleared. Thanks for the help! :tada:

lina (support): Great — marking as resolved. We recommend adding the CiliumNetworkPolicy example to your infra repo and documenting the proxy envs for future clusters.

sam (eng-infra): Follow-up: we'll add a short KB entry listing required egress rules for private deployments. I'll ping you when it's up.

acme-admin: Appreciate it.
